summary: I wanted to tell the story of the space debris and personal items left on the Moon and Mars since the Cold War era (1960s). However, conducting this research was somewhat challenging for me, because in my view, artificial intelligence is not a research source, but a research assistant. Therefore, I decided to design a website both to share the stories of these artifacts and to help like-minded people research them easily. To organize and enrich the information on the website, we developed an AI-powered lunar vehicle: Queen. Queen will first detect the debris from lunar orbit, then land right next to the targets to scan the damage, photograph them, and transmit the data back to Earth.
details:
Project Overview & Purpose

"Silent Witnesses on the Moon and Mars" is a storytelling-driven space exploration and archival project. Since the Cold War era in the 1960s, humanity has left behind tons of spacecraft hardware, rovers, scientific instruments, and deeply personal items on the Moon and Mars. Rather than viewing these remnants merely as space debris, our project treats them as the silent archaeological witnesses of human history. Our goal is to preserve and share the emotional and historical stories behind these artifacts—from Alan Shepard’s golf balls and Charles Duke’s family photograph to the Opportunity rover and Ingenuity helicopter.

How It Works & The Role of "Queen"

To bridge the gap between space archaeology and public accessibility, we designed an interactive web platform supported by our autonomous explorer concept, Queen.

* Orbital Detection: Queen orbits the Moon and Mars to scan and locate manmade artifacts and debris fields.

* Surface Inspection: Upon identifying a target, Queen lands nearby to perform high-resolution damage scans and capture close-up photographs.

* Data Transmission & Storytelling: The collected visual data and historical context are transmitted back to Earth and organized on our website so researchers, students, and space enthusiasts can easily explore them.

Intended Impact & Benefits

* Preserving Space Heritage: Raises global awareness about protecting historic landing sites and artifacts on other celestial bodies.

* Accessible Research: Provides a centralized, easy-to-navigate archive that turns complex space mission records into engaging human stories.

* Ethical AI Philosophy: Demonstrates how artificial intelligence should serve as a research assistant to amplify human curiosity and storytelling, rather than replacing human creativity.

Tools, Software & Development Process

* Web Development & Design: Built and published using Google Sites to ensure a clean, accessible, and responsive archive for global users.

* Media & Presentation: Created visual presentations and promotional video content using Canva and YouTube.

* Research & Data Compilation: Compiled historical mission inventories using official NASA archives (Apollo, LRO, and Mars Exploration Program documentation), assisted by AI tools for structuring, translation, and refinement.
